events.address: Vanderbilt Hall, Grand Central Terminal, 89 E 42nd St, New York, NY 10017
events.what_it_is: A Tatcha skin-and-mind pop-up in Vanderbilt Hall with product discovery, guided and self-guided meditation experiences, and skincare sampling.
events.what_is_free: The pop-up experience, meditation programming and advertised product samples are free. Guided sessions have limited capacity; self-guided meditation spots are also offered by reservation or first-come availability.
events.caveats: Special guided meditation sessions require advance sign-up and space is limited. Self-guided meditation spots are advertised as available by reservation or on a first-come, first-served basis. A stable first-party booking URL was not recovered in this pass, so no RSVP URL is invented.
events.practical_notes: Monday Sept. 21 runs 9 AM–7 PM; Tuesday Sept. 22 runs 8 AM–7 PM. Vanderbilt Hall inside Grand Central Terminal.

events.address: Chief Clubhouse, 13 E 19th St, New York, NY 10003
events.what_it_is: A two-day immersive sustainable-home experience with 70+ mission-driven brands, product activations and sampling, a Gifting Garden, and a main-stage program during Climate Week NYC.
events.what_is_free: Registration is free and includes access to both public event days, including the brand-experience areas and advertised programming.
events.caveats: The official Luma registration page explicitly says registration is subject to host approval. Requesting a spot is not confirmation of admission.
events.practical_notes: Open Sept. 21 and Sept. 22 from 8:30 AM–4 PM each day according to the host registration page. One approved registration includes both days.

events.event_name: Light Hill: Art into Action, Educational Gallery
events.address: Chart Gallery, 74 Franklin St, New York, NY 10013
events.what_it_is: A week-long Climate Week educational gallery pop-up pairing original art with methane-pollution data, maps and tools intended to make otherwise invisible emissions visible.
events.what_is_free: The gallery is explicitly described by the organizer listing as free and open to the public.
events.caveats: The official Climate Week listing offers registration, while the event description also explicitly says the gallery is free and open to the public. No source reviewed states that advance registration is mandatory, so registration is treated as optional rather than required.
events.practical_notes: Open daily Sept. 21–27, 11 AM–6 PM, at Chart Gallery, 74 Franklin Street.
